newsitem.title: USA: FORECAST-Industry up, housing off - Nov 18 wk data.
newsitem.headline: FORECAST-Industry up, housing off - Nov 18 wk data.

text.p: Evidence of continued sluggishness in manufacturing and strength in housing should emerge from next week's U.S. economic calendar, said domestic economists in a Reuters poll.
Many of the 25 experts surveyed on Friday said the Federal Reserve Bank of Philadelphia's business outlook index, set for release next Thursday, tops the thin list of economic events.
"The other data is backward-looking, and Philly Fed is the most up-to-date thing we have," said John Park, an economist at Sanwa Securities USA Co.
On average, the experts forecast the Philadelphia Fed survey dipped to 5.0 in November from 5.3 the month before.
The report should show "a marginal slowdown" in manufacturing, said Kim Rupert, senior economist at MMS International Inc. "There's overall softening, but I think it's a temporary thing."

Another release, Tuesday's Commerce Department report on October housing starts, will reflect continued strength in that sector, the experts said. They forecast starts held rose slightly last month to a 1.443-million-unit annual rate.

"Housing has been amazingly resilient this year given the run-up in rates," said Kevin Flanagan, vice president and an economist at Dean Witter Reynolds Inc. "It could continue to remain a support for the economy."
International trade gets top billing next Wednesday. The trade gap shrank slightly in September to a $9.5 billion deficit from $10.5 billion in August, survey respondents said.
"The trade sector is still a problem for the U.S. economy," Sanwa's Park summed up. "In the fourth quarter it's going to improve, but not by all that much."
